question: Is a bird observed visiting prior to the prospective breeding/first egg period, rather than after chick hatch, and can its first-ever egg attempt be observed in a same-tag nest dataset at t+1? What is the proper denominator when late nonbreeder visits are frequent?

source_time_prior_art.reference: Emmerson Walsh Southwell 2019 Ecology and Evolution
source_time_prior_art.observation: Most nonbreeder weighbridge crossings occurred after chicks hatched, and only relatively few early crossings; up to 150 breeders and 50 nonbreeders per 5-day bin. Two islandwide on-nest tag scans on 23–29 Nov and 11–18 Dec detected >98% of tightly incubating birds, not all nonbreeders.

source_time_prior_art.reference: Acker et al 2022 Journal of Animal Ecology (kittiwakes)
source_time_prior_art.observation: Site-quality attraction and competition influence breeding propensity and status-specific immigration/skip/prebreeder rates. Hypothesis is not novel as a general theory.
Sea-ice-driven reproductive collapse and size-dependent chick post-fledging survival already published.

safety_rules: Only within-INDIVIDUAL season/site phase compare first gate detection (not true arrival) with locally measured earliest egg-laying date and first hatch date, both different uncertain measurements
No universal breeding-season calendar day threshold borrowed from Ross/King George; source Béchervaise site/season and study-specific dates required
Nonbreeding visitors detected AFTER first hatch do not belong to a PRE-egg at-risk gate-entrant denominator; they may prospect for NEXT season but only if tracked next year
An after-hatch adult could theoretically attempt unusually late breeding, so exclusion from prespecified conventional early first-egg cohort is an analytic definition not a proof impossible laying
Repeated passes = one tag-season observation unit; known previous breeders who skip year separated from known-age never breeders
Visible on-nest tag alone != independently egg-confirmed; direct egg date before gate invalidates gate→egg interpretation
An undetected on-nest bird is UNKNOWN after source-specific scan effort; >98% tightly incubating scan detection is NOT sensitivity for nest attendance or all visitors
Unknown tag IDs, missing dates, gate direction and ambiguous egg dates must not be converted into successes/failures
The 2019 original same-ID status analysis is prior art; late nonbreeder timing itself is published, not new
Acker 2022 competition-for-good-patches explanation is prior art even if recreated in penguins; external causal replication needed for island theory

new_estimands_only_if_sources_exist.same_season: P(same adult verified egg after documented EARLY gate pass | first detected pre-egg gate pass, prior attempt status known, adult-at-risk and detection modeled)
new_estimands_only_if_sources_exist.following_season: P(first confirmed egg in season t+1 | known-age tagged juvenile at colony in season t without prior breeding, with separate early and late t visit timings, and subsequent year site search effort documented)
new_estimands_only_if_sources_exist.late_prospecting: descriptive fraction of tagged never-breeders first seen post-hatch who return pre-egg in t+1; this is NOT a causal attractiveness effect
